newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt relaxes foreign bank rules.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt relaxes foreign bank rules.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday it would allow foreign banks to issue securities on the Australian market under changes to the Banking Act.

"The government has decided to provide a general exemption ... to allow foreign domiciled banks to issue, in their own name, securities on Australia's wholesale capital market," Assistant Treasurer Jim Short said in a statement.
He said the measure would lower administrative costs for such banks and enhance their access to Australia's capital market.
Previously, the Australian government insisted that foreign banks issue their securities in Australia through a guaranteed subsidiary company that did not include the word "bank" in its name.
The aim was to minimise confusion as to what constituted a prudentially supervised banking entity in Australia, especially among retail customers.
Short said the exemption would only apply to securities traded in the wholesale market and would be subject to specific disclosure requirements.

Under the exemption, the securities offered must be traded in parcels of more than A$500,000 and it must be clearly stated on the securities that they were issued by a bank that is not authorised under the Banking Act.
The exemption is due to take effect on Wednesday.
